label: heart-s1
summary: The model (training AUC 0.939) is a nearly linear score: replacing its nonlinear units by their affine fits leaves an AUC of 0.937. Its backbone is direct_terms, the inputs' own edges (without it the AUC falls to 0.861): through these edges being male, asymptomatic chest pain, a flat ST slope, more coloured vessels, higher cholesterol, more ST depression and higher resting blood pressure raise predicted risk, while a normal thallium scan, a fixed thallium defect and typical angina lower it. Hidden parts add to this on the logit scale: an always-on unit that lowers the score for the 70 patients with non-anginal chest pain (mean contribution -1.03); a hinge that adds 1.04 on average for the 157 patients with any coloured vessel or a flat ST slope; a hinge on ST depression above a threshold for patients with a normal resting ECG (on for 49 patients); and a vessel-count chain in which a higher maximum heart rate lowers risk slightly once it is high enough. Age is not connected to any node. Worth checking: the model ranks a fixed thallium defect below a normal scan (fitted to 15 patients), and gives a downsloping ST segment the prediction of an upsloping one.
